title: A power saving for planar unit distances
main_claim: There are absolute constants C and beta<4/3 such that every n-point planar set has at most C n^beta unit distances. The proof is by contradiction along a sequence with t^{4-o(1)} incidences: a cutting plus a maximizing rectangle give an expanding incidence piece whose wedges have endpoint mutual information o(log t). That feeds a short-history prediction lemma. The height scale S is the integrated minority fraction of threshold bits of edge jumps over all places. Bounded S is ruled out by a 3-neighbour determinant/Cramer argument at a fresh embedding. If S→∞, product-formula score budgets show common levels are negligible and rare-level point exceptions keep mass ≫S. This yields a dense pair graph whose ratios λ_pr have height ≥J/3 while rectangle products have height o(J). That graph is ruled out algebraically: k_0 (height o(J)) is relatively algebraically closed, a k_0-derivation is nonzero on the ratios, a generic 20x5 grid is chosen, private odd valuations make the radicands independent mod squares, and an unused Kummer sign change gives A=A'_ℓ, a contradiction.

issues.description: Several symbols are reused with different meanings: M (code alphabet size, template count, and the field K_0(p)), lambda (score constant vs edge ratios), eta (expansion exponent 1/25 vs the transfer parameter k^{-1/8}), T (history tests, flank length T_v, the two-prediction score). The meaning is clear in each place and no step depends on mixing them up. This is a readability point, not a mathematical gap.
issues.evidence: bud:template-count defines M<=L^{2Kk}, while pred:acceptance uses M for the alphabet; com:transfer uses 0<eta<1/2 with eta=k^{-1/8}, while Sec. 1 sets eta=1/25.

coverage:
Read all 8 sections in full (about 3800 lines of LaTeX). Steps re-derived by hand:
- Sec. 1: incidence scales; expansion bound inc:expansion with gamma=27/50 (feasible and infeasible cases, xi_t=t^{-a/48}); atom lower bound via (1-x)^gamma<=1-gamma x; matching-label lemma; entropy bound D<=(a+o(a))log t.
- Sec. 2: prediction device (KL chain rule over transcripts, Pinsker, centered residuals, wedge-square identity, constant 4BB'); strict-cross feature inner product; hashing error 4/L.
- Sec. 3: determinant identity (D1-D2)(D1-D3)(D2-D3)/(D1D2D3); Cramer bound 64B^5 tau/r^3<r/2; tail bounds; state-consistency integral O(1).
- Sec. 4: place identity -log|(d-d')(1/d-1/d')|=2alpha-(b'-b); flank intervals; the interval/central-window lemma; constant 4delta^2 lambda/(2(1/4-delta^2))<=10delta^2 lambda; diagonal collision terms; rare lower budget.
- Sec. 5: VC-type double-sampling bound for crosses; transfer lemma (5eta+3eta); exhaustive strict-cross classification in both slice arguments; score polynomial >=lambda/2; T-score product-formula bound, including the role of ht:range at zero-width places; final f<=C(V_P+V_Q) step.
- Sec. 6: pointwise estimate; layer-cake tail bound with Young; profile identity Y=b+sigma(X_p+X_q); band selection; popular-circle cost; rectangle height 4delta_t J.
- Sec. 7: k_0 relatively algebraically closed; derivation existence; differentiated identity and R^2=L(L-4); transcendence-degree count N=20>3j=15; private valuations in the plane, curve, line and fractional cases (discriminant 16(1-b), and the b=1 square identity); Kummer sign-change contradiction, including the collinear/line subcase.
Not independently re-verified: the cited external theorems (Szekely, real-closed-field transfer, Kummer theory, Bezout) and the cutting lemma's region count beyond a plausibility check.
